The campaign's domestic-tragedy chapter. Harry's experimental therapy — a black, fluid-like substance Norman's foundation has been administering — is revealed to Peter as the source of Harry's recovery. The chapter is structured around a sustained sequence at Harry's penthouse, with Peter helping a still-weakened Harry through a flare-up that nearly ends his life. The therapy is administered. Harry recovers. The substance is left in a containment unit Peter accidentally damages.

The chapter ends with the **symbiote bonding to Peter** in his sleep. The first symbiote sequences are staged with deliberate intimacy: Peter's apartment, his bedroom, his slow waking realization that something is moving across his skin. The black suit — the franchise's most iconic alternate costume — manifests for the first time on the chapter's final morning.

The chapter's combat highlights include the **black-suit unlock mission**, in which Peter, now wearing the symbiote, intercepts a Hunter assault on a Brooklyn waterfront warehouse. The new combat system — symbiote tendril attacks, surge meter generation, and the rage-management mechanics that will define Peter's mid-campaign — is fully introduced.

chapters.name: 6. Miles vs. Mister Negative
chapters.summary:
Miles's parallel campaign chapter and one of the campaign's most acclaimed single arcs. **Martin Li** — Mister Negative, the man who killed Miles's father in the original campaign — has been released from prison on parole and has returned to Harlem. The chapter opens with Miles tracking Li through Brooklyn, with the player methodically uncovering Li's apparent reformation: he is working at F.E.A.S.T., he is genuinely helping his community, and his powers are visibly diminished.

The chapter's central question is what Miles will do when he finds him. The campaign refuses easy answers. The combat encounter with Li is staged in a F.E.A.S.T. shelter at night, with Li refusing to defend himself and Miles forced to confront the reality that the man who killed his father is no longer the man who killed his father. The chapter's resolution — Miles's decision to leave Li alive, despite years of grief and rage — is one of the franchise's most emotionally mature scenes.

The chapter ends with Miles returning home to **Rio Morales**, his mother, with the campaign's quietest character beat: the recognition that Miles has grown into something better than his anger.

chapters.name: 7. The Symbiote Spreads — Coney Island
chapters.summary:
The campaign's mid-second-act spectacle chapter. Peter, increasingly affected by the symbiote, accompanies Harry on an outing to **Coney Island** that the campaign frames as nostalgic celebration. The chapter is structured around a sustained Hunters assault on the boardwalk, with the symbiote's full combat suite unleashed for the first time in extended open combat.

The chapter's emotional centerpiece is the deterioration of Peter's character. The symbiote is accelerating his reactions, his power, and his rage. The chapter dwells on his treatment of MJ during the Coney Island sequence — short-tempered, dismissive, increasingly cruel — and the campaign refuses to soften the moments where Peter behaves like someone Mary Jane has every right to be afraid of.

The chapter ends with Kraven's forces pushed back, the campaign's first major Hunters defeat, and Harry's discovery that the symbiote substance has bonded with Peter rather than remaining in containment. The implications are immediately catastrophic.

chapters.name: 8. The Hunt for Sandman — The Black Cat Heist
chapters.summary:
A character-pivot chapter that brings **Felicia Hardy** back into the campaign as a sustained partner. Black Cat has returned to New York to recover the **Sandman crystals** — the substance Sandman's body was reduced to during the opening chapter, now scattered across the city and being collected by Kraven's forces. The chapter is structured as a stealth-heist collaboration, with Peter (in the black suit) and Felicia working through multiple parallel infiltrations across Manhattan rooftops.

The chapter's combat highlights include the campaign's most sustained sequence of partner-coordinated takedowns, with Felicia's grapple line and Peter's symbiote tendrils combining in ways the franchise has not previously staged. The chapter dwells on the friction between Felicia's pragmatic moral framework and Peter's increasingly symbiote-driven anger.

The chapter ends with the Sandman crystals recovered, Felicia leaving New York permanently, and Peter's slow recognition that he can no longer control the symbiote's influence on his behavior.

chapters.name: 9. The Black Suit Confrontation
chapters.summary:
The campaign's emotional pivot. MJ — alongside Miles and a recovering Harry — stages an intervention in Peter's apartment after a violent incident at the substitute-teaching job has resulted in Peter physically assaulting a student. The chapter is structured as a sustained character confrontation, with no combat, no music, and Yuri Lowenthal's performance landing the campaign's most disturbing scene as Peter resists every attempt to remove the symbiote.

The chapter's emotional crescendo is the **church bell sequence** — the franchise's canonical method of separating Peter from the symbiote, staged at a Brooklyn cathedral with Miles fighting the symbiote-controlled Peter across the bell tower. The symbiote is removed. Peter survives. The substance flees into the cathedral's understructure.

The chapter ends with Harry, weakened by the symbiote's departure from Peter's body, returning to his Foundation containment unit — where the substance, drawn back to its original host, finds him. The campaign's third-act antagonist is born.

chapters.name: 10. Venom Awakens
chapters.summary:
The campaign's third-act opening. **Harry Osborn** is now bonded to the symbiote at significantly deeper levels than Peter ever was. The chapter is structured as a citywide outbreak sequence — Harry, now calling himself **Venom**, has begun spreading the symbiote across Manhattan via a controlled infection vector, with the substance bonding to civilians and transforming them into symbiote-controlled drones.

The chapter's combat highlights are the campaign's most apocalyptic. Symbiote-infected citizens swarm the streets, the East River crossings collapse under the weight of fleeing civilians, and Spider-Man (both Peter and Miles) is forced to fight through populations of people who cannot be killed but cannot be safely captured.

The chapter ends with Harry's symbiote army established across Manhattan, the city's infrastructure collapsing, and Norman Osborn arriving on the scene with the campaign's most surprising character pivot: his recognition that his son has become a monster he himself created.

chapters.name: 11. The Symbiote Invasion
chapters.summary:
The campaign's largest open-world sequence and one of the most ambitious single chapters Insomniac has ever staged. The entire Manhattan map is now infected with symbiote infrastructure — black tendrils growing from buildings, swarmed pedestrians, and Kraven's surviving Hunters joining the battle as a third faction. The chapter is structured as a sustained, multi-objective response across the city.

The chapter's combat highlights include the **Anti-Venom suit acquisition** — the unique mid-third-act unlock that gives Peter the only weapon capable of meaningfully damaging Harry. The Anti-Venom mechanics are staged across multiple late-game encounters, with healing-while-attacking systems that redefine the franchise's combat math.

The chapter ends with the campaign's central question fully posed: in order to save Harry, Peter and Miles will have to defeat him decisively, and the substance bonded to his body may not survive the separation.

chapters.name: 12. The Final Confrontation — Venom
chapters.summary:
The campaign's climactic boss fight. **Venom** has retreated to the top of an Oscorp building in midtown, where his final transformation is reaching its apex. The chapter is structured as a multi-stage co-op battle, with Peter (in Anti-Venom suit) and Miles (in his full Venom-Strike loadout) alternating phases of the encounter.

The fight is the largest-scale boss confrontation Insomniac has shipped. Venom uses every symbiote ability the campaign has staged at exponentially larger scale — citywide tendrils, civilian-shield manipulation, and a final transformation into a colossal symbiote leviathan that drags the rooftop arena across the Manhattan skyline. The fight ends with Peter and Miles cornering Harry, separating him from the symbiote, and the substance dispersed.

The chapter ends with Harry comatose, the symbiote contained, and the city beginning the long recovery from the invasion.

chapters.name: 13. New Beginnings — Epilogue
chapters.summary:
The campaign's epilogue weaves multiple character arcs into closing position. Peter retires from the Spider-Man identity — committed to caring for the comatose Harry full-time and to repairing his relationship with Mary Jane. Miles is left as **New York's primary Spider-Man**, a role the campaign explicitly frames as Miles's by right and by capability. Felicia, Yuri, and the returning supporting cast are positioned for the franchise's continuation.

The chapter's post-credits scenes establish the next decade of the franchise. **Mister Negative** is moved to permanent isolation. **Cindy Moon** — a longtime supporting character — receives her own Spider-related origin in a sequence the campaign teases without resolving. And in the chapter's final shot, **Norman Osborn**, alone in his office, reaches for a containment vial that the audience knows contains the seed of the next campaign's central threat.

story:
Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is Insomniac Games' 2023 PS5-exclusive direct sequel to *Marvel's Spider-Man (2018)* and *Spider-Man: Miles Morales (2020)*, structurally the bridge that has carried the franchise's two Spider-Men into shared continuity. The previous installments established **Peter Parker** as New York's elder Spider-Man with eight years of experience, **Miles Morales** as his fully-trained successor still finding his own approach to the role, and the broader Insomniac Marvel continuity's central villain network — Otto Octavius incarcerated at the Raft, Norman Osborn as the city's mayor with no public knowledge of his son Harry's Greek-coma medical situation, and Mr. Negative dismantled but not destroyed. Spider-Man 2 picks up roughly ten months later.

The opening sequence stages the franchise's first sustained dual-Spider-Man cooperation as Peter and Miles intervene against a deliberately-staged attack on the city by the mercenary **Sandman**. The opening battle introduces the campaign's dual-protagonist combat system — instant switching between Peter and Miles in the world map's open-zone exploration — and establishes the city's broader political infrastructure. The campaign's central reveal lands in the opening hour: **Harry Osborn**, Peter's lifelong best friend, has been revived from his medical coma by his father Norman through an experimental alien organism Norman has acquired via a secretive Oscorp acquisition. The organism is the **Venom Symbiote**.

The campaign's middle act develops three converging threads. **Kraven the Hunter** — a Russian aristocratic hunter dying of a terminal illness — has come to New York for a Most-Dangerous-Game-style hunt of the city's superhuman population, with his explicit goal being his own death at the hands of a worthy opponent. Kraven's hunt provides the campaign's central action structure. **Peter's gradual corruption by the Venom Symbiote** — initially provided to him by Harry as a therapeutic healing modality after a critical Kraven-inflicted wound — drives the campaign's psychological arc, with Peter becoming progressively aggressive, paranoid, and emotionally cruel toward MJ, Miles, and Aunt May. **Miles's parallel pursuit of Martin Li** — the previous game's Mr. Negative antagonist, now in custody and facing trial — anchors the campaign's continuity-grounding character work.

The campaign's structural climax lands in two converging beats. **Venom decapitates Kraven** in the most acclaimed mid-game sequence — the Symbiote, separated from Peter through Miles's intervention, has rebonded with Harry and consumed his sense of self. Harry, now the campaign's true Venom, escapes Oscorp's containment infrastructure and begins systematically bonding the Symbiote with the city's broader civilian population through an airborne reproductive deployment. The campaign's third-act spectacle is the city's mass-conversion sequence — **Mary Jane is bonded to a derived Symbiote** in one of the franchise's most acclaimed character beats, becoming the temporary antagonist **Scream**. The protagonists' coordinated response involves Martin Li's negotiated cooperation in severing Peter's residual Symbiote connection — a process that grants Peter the **Anti-Venom** powers the franchise's broader comic continuity has long maintained.

The climactic sequence stages the dual-Spider-Man confrontation with the fully-realized Venom. Harry is the central tragedy the campaign refuses to soften: the same medical intervention that saved his life has transformed him into the city's most dangerous threat. The Spider-Men disable Venom at Oscorp Tower's central reactor — Harry is left in a permanent deep coma, the Symbiote contained but not destroyed, the campaign's central emotional resolution deliberately bittersweet. The campaign's epilogue stages Peter's quiet decision to step back from the Spider-Man identity in order to spend his time with MJ and to support Harry's continuing care. Miles accepts the city's full protective responsibility. Two post-credits stingers position the franchise's third installment: Norman Osborn visits Otto Octavius at the Raft to recruit him for a planned **"final act"** against the Spider-Men; and Miles's mother introduces her new boyfriend's daughter **Cindy Moon** — the franchise's seeded protagonist Silk — for the broader continuity's continuation.

title: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales
guide: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales is the standalone Insomniac follow-up to the 2018 original, following Miles Morales' first solo Spider-Man Christmas in a snow-covered Harlem. Peter Parker is away in Europe so Miles takes up the mantle alone against the Tinkerer and the Roxxon Energy corporation. The walkthrough captures the full main campaign on PS5 Pro at 4K HDR 60FPS with PSSR upscaling, no commentary.

chapters.name: 1. Be Yourself
chapters.summary:
The campaign opens with a sustained highway pursuit sequence in which **Miles Morales** — newly trained by Peter Parker — escorts a Department of Damage Control transport carrying **Rhino** through Manhattan. The chapter is structured as the franchise's most spectacle-heavy opening, with Miles and Peter working in tandem across an extended high-speed chase that demonstrates Miles's distinct combat identity (bio-electric Venom Strike attacks, camouflage stealth) before introducing the campaign's central tragedy.

The chapter ends with Peter Parker leaving New York for a vacation with MJ in Europe, formally entrusting the city's protection to Miles for the campaign's duration. The chapter's emotional pivot is Miles's growing sense that he must define himself on his own terms rather than as Peter's apprentice.

chapters.name: 2. Welcome Home — Harlem
chapters.summary:
The campaign's hub introduction. Miles moves with his mother **Rio Morales** into a new apartment in **Harlem**, the neighborhood that will serve as the campaign's primary open-world space. The chapter weaves combat against street-level crime with the establishment of Miles's social network — his uncle **Aaron Davis**, his best friend **Ganke Lee**, and the broader Harlem community.

The chapter introduces the campaign's central political backdrop. **Rio Morales** is running for City Council on an anti-Roxxon platform, with **Roxxon Energy Corporation** having begun a controversial energy-research facility in the neighborhood. The Roxxon Plaza tower has become the chapter's primary villain — visible from every Harlem street, casting permanent shadow over the community.

The chapter ends with the first sightings of **the Underground**, a Harlem-based resistance movement whose tactics against Roxxon have escalated into open street combat.

chapters.name: 3. Roxxon Plaza — First Investigation
chapters.summary:
The campaign's first sustained antagonist confrontation. Miles infiltrates **Roxxon Plaza** to investigate reports of unauthorized human experimentation. The chapter is structured as a multi-stage stealth-and-combat sequence through the tower's research wings, with the campaign's first sustained encounter with both Roxxon's private security forces and the Underground's masked operatives.

The chapter introduces **Simon Krieger**, Roxxon's CEO, as the campaign's primary corporate antagonist. Krieger's public-facing reformist message — that Roxxon's experimental energy research will benefit Harlem — is set against the chapter's revealed reality of forced human testing and political bribery. The chapter ends with Miles's first sighting of **the Tinkerer**, the Underground's masked leader, who escapes the rooftop confrontation with Krieger's stolen prototype.

chapters.name: 4. The Underground — Phin's Connection
chapters.summary:
The campaign's character pivot. The chapter reveals that **the Tinkerer** is **Phin Mason** — Miles's childhood best friend, who he hasn't seen since her brother **Rick Mason** died working for Roxxon. The chapter is structured as a series of flashback sequences interleaved with present-day combat, with Phin's grief over Rick's death establishing the campaign's central emotional conflict.

The chapter dwells on the moral weight of the Underground's mission. Phin's faction is fighting for genuine justice — Rick's death was preventable, Roxxon's energy research is killing people, and the corporate response has been bribery and threats. Miles's role as Spider-Man is the chapter's central question: he is sworn to protect the city, but the city's actual enemy is the corporation his mother is running against.

The chapter ends with Miles and Phin's first confrontation as Spider-Man versus the Tinkerer, with both refusing to back down from their respective causes.

chapters.name: 5. Family History — Aaron Davis Revealed
chapters.summary:
The campaign's emotional pivot. Miles discovers that his uncle **Aaron Davis** is **the Prowler** — a high-end thief working for Roxxon's intelligence operations, including the surveillance program that tracked Rick Mason before his death. The chapter is structured as a sustained confrontation in the Davis family's Harlem apartment, with the moral weight of the revelation landing on Miles's relationship with the man who has been his most consistent adult mentor.

The chapter dwells on Aaron's motivations. He has been working for Roxxon to support the family financially after Rio's late husband Jefferson's death; his thefts have funded Miles's tuition and Rio's political campaign. The chapter's central question — whether complicity is forgivable when the alternative is family destitution — is left explicitly open.

The chapter ends with Aaron arrested by NYPD as Miles watches from across the street, the family's secret revealed publicly, and Rio's political campaign now compromised by the connection.

chapters.name: 6. The Tinkerer Revealed — The Underground's Plan
chapters.summary:
The campaign's second-act pivot. **Phin Mason** publicly reveals her identity as the Tinkerer in a coordinated assault on Roxxon Plaza. The chapter is structured as a citywide combat sequence, with the Underground deploying weaponized technology against Roxxon's private security across multiple districts.

The chapter's central reveal is the **Nuform crisis**. The Underground has stolen Krieger's experimental Nuform energy reactor, which Phin intends to detonate in Roxxon Plaza as both vengeance and a demonstration. The detonation would destroy the tower — and likely most of Harlem alongside it. The chapter dwells on Phin's emotional state: she has known about the Nuform's instability all along, and she has been willing to accept the casualties.

The chapter ends with the Underground's planning fully exposed, Phin committed to the detonation, and Miles racing across the city to prevent the catastrophe.

chapters.name: 7. The Roxxon Plaza Assault
chapters.summary:
The campaign's spectacle-heavy mid-third-act chapter. Miles infiltrates Roxxon Plaza during the active Underground assault, with the chapter weaving sustained combat against both factions simultaneously. The chapter introduces the campaign's most demanding combat encounters, with Krieger's Roxxon enforcers deploying anti-Spider-Man weaponry and the Underground's operatives using bio-electric counter-tech.

The chapter dwells on the campaign's central moral compromise. Miles must defeat both factions — the corporate antagonist whose villainy created the crisis, and the rebellion whose response will kill thousands of innocent people. The campaign refuses to grant Miles a clean victory in either direction.

The chapter ends with Krieger captured by Miles, the Roxxon Plaza tower partially evacuated, and Phin still committed to the Nuform detonation despite her allies' second thoughts.

chapters.name: 8. Brooklyn Bridge — The Final Chase
chapters.summary:
The campaign's vertical action set-piece. Phin, in possession of the Nuform reactor, attempts to detonate it at maximum altitude over Brooklyn Bridge to maximize the damage radius. The chapter is structured as a sustained aerial pursuit, with Miles using his expanded Venom-Strike repertoire to chase Phin across the bridge's superstructure.

The chapter's emotional pivot is the final confrontation. Miles catches Phin mid-flight, and the conversation that follows — staged on the bridge's central span — refuses every easy resolution. Phin is not a villain. She is a grieving sister whose city has refused justice. Miles is not a clean hero. His family has been complicit in the system that killed her brother.

The chapter ends with Phin's sacrifice. She chooses to fly the Nuform reactor far enough into the atmosphere that its detonation will not harm Harlem, dying in the explosion to give the city the safety her brother never received. Miles's grief is the campaign's emotional climax.

chapters.name: 9. Aftermath — Penn Station
chapters.summary:
The campaign's epilogue chapter. The detonation's shockwave has damaged Penn Station and surrounding infrastructure. The chapter is structured as a sustained civilian-rescue sequence across Harlem and Midtown, with Miles using his full Spider-Man toolkit to evacuate trapped commuters and stabilize the damaged buildings.

The chapter dwells on the campaign's quiet emotional resolution. **Rio Morales** wins her City Council race. **Aaron Davis** accepts his sentence with dignity. **Ganke** processes the loss of Phin alongside Miles. The chapter ends with Miles standing on a Harlem rooftop, formally accepting the Spider-Man identity as his own — not as Peter Parker's apprentice but as the protector of his own neighborhood.

chapters.name: 10. The Hero of Harlem — Epilogue
chapters.summary:
The campaign's final chapter is staged across a sustained day in Miles's life as Harlem's Spider-Man. The chapter weaves several small open-world activities with the campaign's character resolutions — Miles's growing relationship with **Hailey Cooper**, a deaf Brooklyn Visions student; his deepening bond with his mother; and his commitment to the neighborhood he has now formally adopted as his domain.

The chapter's final scene is a video call between Miles and Peter (returning from Europe), with Peter formally recognizing Miles as a full Spider-Man rather than an apprentice. The credits roll over Miles's first sustained swing through Harlem at sunset, with the campaign's central question — who Miles Morales is as a hero — answered in the only way the franchise permits: on his own terms.

story:
Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales is Insomniac Games' 2020 PS5 launch-window standalone sequel to *Marvel's Spider-Man (2018)*, set roughly **one year after** Peter Parker's confrontation with the Sinister Six. The previous installment closed with **Miles Morales** — a Harlem-raised teenager whose own spider-bite incident occurred in the closing minutes — receiving Peter's mentorship as the city's second Spider-Man. The standalone sequel is the franchise's foregrounding of Miles as a central protagonist in his own right, with the campaign's runtime, structure, and character work fully committed to his individual arc separate from Peter's previous central role.

The campaign opens at the **winter holiday season**, with Miles and his mother **Rio Morales** preparing for the family's relocation back to Harlem after a year of residence on the city's Lower East Side. Peter is departing for Europe with MJ on a journalism assignment, and the city's surviving Spider-Man protective infrastructure will be entirely Miles's responsibility for the campaign's duration. The opening sequence stages a sustained Rikers Island prison-transport hijacking by **Rhino**, with Peter and Miles's coordinated response introducing the campaign's combat system. Peter's departure for Europe immediately follows; Miles is the city's only Spider-Man for the next several weeks.

The campaign's central political conflict is the corporate-versus-resistance contest in Miles's Harlem neighborhood. **Roxxon Energy Corporation**, a multinational energy conglomerate, has been deploying a new energy infrastructure called **Nuform** across the city's underserved neighborhoods — including Harlem, where Roxxon's central reactor is being installed over significant community objection. The resistance organization opposing Roxxon's deployment is the **Underground**, a masked vigilante coalition led by the engineering figure called the **Tinkerer**. Miles, initially sympathetic to the Underground's stated cause, gradually discovers that the Tinkerer's broader strategic position requires increasingly violent escalation against Roxxon's civilian infrastructure.

The campaign's central reveal lands at the midpoint. The Tinkerer is **Phin Mason**, Miles's closest childhood friend, who has been pursuing a personal vendetta against Roxxon for the death of her older brother **Rick Mason**. Rick was a Roxxon engineer who had been developing the Nuform infrastructure with Phin's support; when Rick recognized that Nuform's instability would have catastrophic consequences for the broader neighborhood and attempted to expose the project's safety concerns publicly, he was killed by Roxxon's enforcement agent **Krieger**. Phin's broader Underground operation has been a coordinated revenge plan, with the final stage being the destruction of Roxxon's central Harlem reactor as a public demonstration of Nuform's actual dangers — at the cost of catastrophic civilian casualties across Harlem.

The climactic sequence stages Miles's coordinated response to Phin's reactor-detonation operation. He defeats her in single combat in the reactor's central control room. He attempts to absorb the unstable Nuform energy with his **Venom Blast** powers as a containment measure. The energy accumulation rapidly exceeds his physiological capacity. Phin, recognizing in the final moments that her vendetta has positioned her best friend for his own death, lifts Miles into the New York airspace and uses her own enhanced flight capability to position him for a controlled release that will kill her in his place. Miles's release of the absorbed Nuform energy is staged in slow motion against the city skyline; Phin is incinerated in the discharge. The campaign closes with Miles placing the science award he and Phin won together in middle school atop **Trinity Church** as a private memorial, and a sustained nighttime phone call with his mother Rio in which he processes his conflicted grief about a friend whose violent vendetta he respected as morally legitimate even as he had to stop her. The post-credits stinger positions the broader Insomniac Marvel continuity for *Marvel's Spider-Man 2*'s dual-Spider-Man framework.

title: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered
guide: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered is the PS5 enhanced edition of the 2018 original, with rebuilt facial capture, improved lighting, and ray-traced reflections across Manhattan. Peter Parker has been Spider-Man for eight years and balances superheroics with his day job at Otto Octavius's lab. The walkthrough captures the full main campaign across two parts on PS5 Pro at 4K HDR 60FPS with PSSR upscaling, no commentary.

chapters.name: 1. The Fall of Fisk
chapters.summary:
The campaign's opening hour is structured as a tutorial wrapped in one of the franchise's most confident introductions. Peter Parker — now twenty-three, eight years into his career as Spider-Man, and in the middle of an eighteen-month investigation — finally has actionable intel on crime lord **Wilson Fisk**'s penthouse fortress at the top of Fisk Tower. The chapter opens with Spider-Man's iconic swing across the Financial District, accompanied by the John Paesano score, and immediately establishes the traversal system as one of the most physically convincing in any superhero game.

The Fisk Tower infiltration introduces every major combat verb in sequence: melee fundamentals, web-shooter combinations, the perfect-dodge Spider-Sense system, perch takedowns, stealth web-strikes from environmental hooks, and the gadget loadout. The level design escalates floor by floor, ending in a wrecked penthouse where Fisk himself charges Spider-Man in a multi-phase brawl. The Kingpin fight is mechanically simple but thematically loaded — Fisk is positioned as a man whose only response to anything is brute force, and the fight is staged around dodging his linear charges while clearing reinforcement waves.

The chapter closes with Fisk in custody, the NYPD on the rooftop, and Peter's voice-over warning that whatever was holding the city's underworld in check is now gone. The first **Inner Demons** are sighted in the closing montage, planting the antagonist seed that will dominate the rest of Act 1.

chapters.name: 2. The Inner Demons Rise
chapters.summary:
The early hours of Act 1 open the city map fully and introduce the Inner Demons as the campaign's first proper enemy faction. The Demons are masked, wear ornate red-and-black armor, and wield neural-corrupted weapons that mark them as something fundamentally more dangerous than the gang remnants of Fisk's empire. Their attacks on former Fisk holdings — clearing penthouses, executing officers, taking territory — establish the chapter's tone of escalation.

The chapter's mid-section is dedicated to the **Yuri Watanabe partnership**, the player's introduction to Captain Yuri at the 84th Precinct. Yuri's tutorial mission at a captured police station weaves stealth fundamentals into the open-world structure: perch takedowns from above, environmental web-strikes, and the alert-cascade mechanic that punishes loud play. The Yuri partnership becomes the campaign's primary law-enforcement thread.

The chapter introduces the campaign's first major boss encounter outside the main story — the **Shocker stakeout**. Shocker's shield-shockwave pattern and the debris-throwing counter establish the design template that the campaign's later bosses will riff on. The chapter closes with the first Demon Bases unlocking on the open-world map, opening combat-arena side content for the rest of the game.

chapters.name: 3. The Daily Bugle
chapters.summary:
A character-focused chapter that brings **Mary Jane Watson** back into the campaign's main thread. MJ, now a senior investigative journalist at the *Daily Bugle*, has been tracking the same Inner Demons crisis from a journalistic angle, and her return positions her as the campaign's secondary playable lead. Her introduction is staged across a Bugle newsroom sequence, a rooftop conversation with Peter, and her first stealth mission infiltrating a Demon storage facility.

The MJ stealth missions are the campaign's most divisive design choice and one of its most thematically intentional. MJ has no combat capabilities, no super powers, and no Spider-Sense — what she has instead is a smartphone camera that marks enemies, a stash of distractions (bottles, pebbles), and a network of cover and patrol patterns to thread through. The first MJ sequence is staged inside an abandoned Demon warehouse, and the failure-restart pacing forces the player to learn the patrol logic carefully.

The chapter ends with MJ recovering the first concrete intelligence on Mister Negative — a name, a corrupted-energy signature, and a connection to F.E.A.S.T. The thread is left dangling for Act 2 to pick up.

chapters.name: 4. Octavius Industries
chapters.summary:
The chapter that anchors the campaign's emotional center. Peter's day job — working as a research assistant for **Dr. Otto Octavius** at Octavius Industries — is introduced in full, with the prosthetic-arm puzzle that doubles as the campaign's first lab minigame. The neural-prosthetic project that Otto and Peter are working on is positioned as an act of genuine scientific idealism — Otto wants to help amputees regain function, and the project is genuinely revolutionary.

The chapter's central conflict is **Mayor Norman Osborn**'s political pressure on Otto. Osborn, Otto's former research partner, has just defunded the entire project, and his on-camera explanation — broadcast in news clips throughout Manhattan — frames Otto as a failed scientist who could not deliver results. Otto's quiet response, staged in the lab's cracked-window office, is one of the campaign's most carefully written scenes.

The chapter introduces the **circuit puzzle** and **molecule synthesis** minigames that will recur throughout the campaign's collectibles and research stations. Peter's growing trust in Otto, his sense of obligation, and his gradual realization that Otto is starting to break — all are seeded here. The chapter ends with Peter walking out of the lab and back into his Spider-Man life, with the campaign's tragedy already underway behind him.

chapters.name: 5. The First Negative Encounter
chapters.summary:
The campaign's first direct confrontation with **Mister Negative**. The chapter is staged across a multi-block Demon assault in midtown, with corrupted-energy attacks tearing through Times Square and Spider-Man arriving to find a fully transformed Negative leading the assault personally. The level design escalates from open-world traversal to a closed-arena boss fight against Negative at the chapter's midpoint.

The first Mister Negative encounter is mechanically designed to be unwinnable — Negative teleports, throws corrupted-energy waves, summons Demon reinforcements faster than Spider-Man can clear them, and ultimately escapes after a punishing exchange. The fight is staged to teach the player that Negative is not a normal villain. The player is expected to lose ground throughout, and the cutscene resolution explicitly frames Spider-Man as outmatched.

The chapter's closing minutes pivot to the **Black Cat stakeouts** — Felicia Hardy's calling cards begin appearing on rooftops, planting the seeds of the post-game DLC arc. The chapter ends with Yuri Watanabe demanding Spider-Man take Negative seriously, and Peter walking out of the precinct with Mister Negative now on his personal hunt list.

chapters.name: 6. F.E.A.S.T. and Miles Morales
chapters.summary:
A narrative-focused chapter that introduces two of the campaign's most important supporting characters. The first is **Martin Li**, the philanthropist who founded the F.E.A.S.T. homeless shelter where Aunt May volunteers — the player has already encountered Mister Negative, and the chapter dwells in the dramatic-irony space of knowing that the soft-spoken Li is the man Spider-Man has been hunting. The shelter scenes are staged with warmth, including a quiet conversation between Peter and May about whether she should retire from active volunteer work.

The chapter's second introduction is **Miles Morales**, the teenager whose family Aunt May has been mentoring through F.E.A.S.T.'s programs. Miles's father, **Officer Jefferson Davis**, is introduced as a working-class NYPD cop with deep loyalty to the shelter and to Mayor Osborn's reformist policies. The Davis family is established as decent, working-class, and quietly important. The chapter does not yet kill any of them.

A side mission inside the chapter has Spider-Man tracking down a warehouse fire that turns out to be a Demon attack on a F.E.A.S.T. supply depot. The fight is the chapter's combat centerpiece. The chapter closes with Peter introducing himself to Miles at the shelter as Aunt May's "friend Peter," and the audience knowing what Miles will eventually become.

chapters.name: 7. Marked Man
chapters.summary:
The campaign's first major narrative pivot. Mister Negative launches a public, coordinated attack on a political event hosted by Mayor Norman Osborn. The chapter's central set-piece is staged across the rooftops surrounding the event and on the public stage itself. Mister Negative's grievance is finally articulated in full — a years-old Oscorp experiment ruined Li's family, and Li blames Osborn personally. The attack is intended to kill Osborn on live television.

The chapter's centerpiece is the **second Mister Negative duel**, fought on an open-air rooftop against the falling debris of the event. Negative is faster, his corrupted-energy walls cut through the arena, and his charged attacks demand perfect-dodge timing the campaign has only just begun to teach. The fight ends mid-sequence as Negative breaks off to commit the chapter's defining act.

That act is the **death of Officer Jefferson Davis**. Davis is killed protecting Osborn during the public attack, in a sequence staged with deliberate weight and no music. The death is the campaign's emotional pivot — it transforms Miles Morales's family from background detail into the campaign's central tragedy, and it commits the player to whatever the next act delivers. The chapter ends with Aunt May breaking the news to Miles's mother **Rio** at F.E.A.S.T., and the city in mourning.

chapters.name: 8. Devil's Breath Unleashed
chapters.summary:
The chapter that opens Act 3. Mister Negative, his political assassination foiled, pivots to the larger plan he has been preparing the entire campaign: the release of **Devil's Breath**, an Oscorp-engineered bioweapon, into Manhattan's water supply. The chapter is structured as a citywide crisis sequence, with Spider-Man racing across districts trying to contain the initial release while the death toll climbs in news broadcasts.

The chapter intercuts Peter's Spider-Man work with Otto Octavius's parallel descent. Otto, devastated by Osborn's betrayal and the failure of his life's work, has been quietly building four mechanical tentacles in his off-campus workshop. The tentacle prototypes are revealed in a sequence staged in a half-lit garage, with Otto's voice still soft, still measured, still recognizably Peter's mentor — and clearly preparing to do something terrible.

The chapter introduces **Aunt May's infection**. Working at F.E.A.S.T. during the initial release, May is one of thousands exposed before the public quarantine. Her diagnosis is delivered in a hospital scene that the campaign will pay off explicitly in its final hour. The chapter closes with the city under martial law, Mister Negative still at large, and Otto's transformation complete.

chapters.name: 9. The Raft Breakout
chapters.summary:
The campaign's most acclaimed mid-game sequence. Doctor Octopus — Otto Octavius now fully transformed — breaks into **The Raft**, the maximum-security island prison off the coast of Manhattan, and releases the **Sinister Six**: Electro, Vulture, Rhino, Scorpion, and Mister Negative. The chapter is structured as a continuous descent through the Raft's containment levels, with each Sinister Six member introduced via their breakout cinematic.

The chapter's defining moment is Spider-Man's first encounter with Doctor Octopus. The fight is mechanically scripted — Doc Ock has total environmental control, can throw concrete pillars at Spider-Man, and is functionally invulnerable to direct attack. The player is forced to lose. The cinematic that follows the staged defeat — **Otto's "I've known all along"** identity reveal — is one of the franchise's defining moments. The reveal recontextualizes the entire campaign: every mentor scene, every lab session, every quiet conversation has been with a man who has been planning this.

The chapter closes with the Sinister Six scattering across Manhattan, the city's largest threat in decades unleashed, and Spider-Man broken on the Raft floor with no clear plan for what comes next.

chapters.name: 10. The Sinister Six Hunt
chapters.summary:
The campaign's mid-third-act open hunt. Spider-Man recovers, returns to Manhattan, and begins hunting the Sinister Six members across the city. The chapter is structured as a hub mission with multiple paths — the player can engage the villains in any order, though the campaign nudges toward a specific sequence.

The chapter's two major boss encounters are the tag-team fights with **Electro and Vulture** and with **Rhino and Scorpion**. The Electro/Vulture duel is staged in Times Square at night, with Vulture using the city's vertical space and Electro chaining lightning across the ground. The Rhino/Scorpion fight takes place in the Financial District, with Rhino's charge attacks forcing the player to learn environmental staggers and Scorpion's hallucinogenic venom distorting the screen with each hit. Both fights are designed to feel like genuine super-villain confrontations rather than reskinned grunt encounters.

The chapter closes with four of the six Sinister Six members in custody, Negative and Doc Ock still at large, and Aunt May's condition worsening at the hospital. The campaign begins its march toward the finale.

chapters.name: 11. The Heart of the Matter
chapters.summary:
The final Mister Negative encounter. The chapter opens with Spider-Man tracking Negative through a citywide helicopter chase, with corrupted-energy attacks raining from the helicopter and the player pursuing in pure swing-traversal mode. The chase ends on a rooftop arena, where Negative makes his final stand in a three-phase boss fight.

The fight is staged across a vertical arena, with each phase forcing the player to relearn Negative's combo strings. Phase 1 is the corrupted-energy moveset the campaign has been teaching since Act 1; phase 2 accelerates everything; phase 3 transforms Negative into a full Inner Demon form, with full-screen AOE attacks that punish anything but perfect-dodge mastery. The fight is the campaign's most pure mechanical exam outside the final battle.

The chapter closes with Negative defeated and Martin Li, finally stripped of his powers, broken on the rooftop. The man Aunt May still believes is a hero is taken into custody, and Peter — for the first time in the campaign — fully understands what the death of Officer Davis cost, and what kind of cost the campaign is still going to demand of him.

chapters.name: 12. The Oscorp Tower Battle
chapters.summary:
The campaign's climactic confrontation. **Doctor Octopus** has barricaded himself at the top of Oscorp Tower with the only doses of antiserum to the Devil's Breath pathogen — including the one that could save Aunt May. The chapter is structured as a vertical assault: Spider-Man fights his way up the tower against Doc Ock's tentacle traps and Sinister Six remnants, then engages Otto himself in the campaign's signature multi-phase boss fight.

The Doc Ock final battle is one of the most acclaimed boss encounters of the past console generation. Stage 1 is staged on the upper terrace with Otto on the ground, his tentacles slamming the arena and creating windows for Spider-Man to web-strike each tentacle when it embeds. Stage 2 transitions into a vertical tower-climb sequence, with Spider-Man wall-running upward as Otto throws debris and tentacles from below. Stage 3 returns to the rooftop with Otto fully unleashed, all four tentacles attacking simultaneously, and the campaign's hardest combo strings forcing perfect-dodge sequences and gadget management.

The chapter's emotional payoff is Otto's defeat. Stripped of his tentacle harness, broken on the rooftop, the man who taught Peter is finally just a man — and a man Peter loves. Otto's last words to Peter, staged in a quiet exchange before the police arrive, complete the campaign's most heartbreaking arc.

chapters.name: 13. The Sacrifice
chapters.summary:
The campaign's epilogue and its emotional climax. Spider-Man returns to the hospital with the recovered antiserum, only to discover that there is exactly one dose left — and that dozens of patients, including Aunt May, are dying citywide. Aunt May, fully aware of the math, chooses to give the dose to the city rather than to herself. The chapter is structured as a single extended dialogue between Peter and May at her bedside.

The conversation reveals that **May has always known Peter is Spider-Man**. She tells him she has been proud of him. She gives him permission to let her go. The scene is staged with no music, in long takes, with both performances — Yuri Lowenthal's Peter and Nancy Linari's May — landing among the most acclaimed in any PlayStation game.

The chapter closes with the campaign's epilogue. Peter and Mary Jane reconcile on a Manhattan rooftop. The city begins to recover. And in Peter's apartment, in the final scene before the credits, **Miles Morales** reveals that he, too, was bitten — and that he, too, now has powers. The line *"I think it's time we had a talk"* sets up the next decade of the franchise.

story:
Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered is Insomniac Games' 2020 PS5 remaster of the 2018 PS4 original — the foundational entry of the studio's Marvel continuity, set roughly **eight years** into Peter Parker's superhero career and structurally committed to a more experienced, established Spider-Man than the franchise's previous adaptations. The campaign opens with Peter as a working scientific researcher at Octavius Industries — Dr. **Otto Octavius's** privately-funded biomechanical prosthetics laboratory — and as an underemployed thirty-something whose Spider-Man identity is increasingly difficult to reconcile with his civilian financial obligations. The opening sequence stages Peter's coordinated arrest of **Wilson Fisk** — Kingpin, the city's central organized-crime figure — after a year-long Spider-Man investigation. The arrest creates the campaign's foundational political instability: Fisk's incarceration produces a power vacuum that the campaign's broader antagonist network systematically exploits.

The campaign's middle act develops three parallel threads. **Peter's relationship with Mary Jane Watson** — a Daily Bugle investigative journalist whose previous relationship with Peter ended over his secret identity — is rebuilt through her own playable investigation chapters into the broader political conspiracy. **Otto Octavius's research collaboration with Peter** is rendered with sustained character intimacy: Otto is the campaign's central mentor figure, his commitment to using prosthetics technology for paralyzed-veterans rehabilitation framed with explicit moral weight, and his slow corruption into the franchise's central antagonist staged with the campaign's most acclaimed character work. **Norman Osborn's mayoral administration** — corrupt, increasingly authoritarian, with private medical research programs that have produced his son Harry's medical coma — is the campaign's broader political backdrop.

The campaign's central reveal lands in the middle hours. **Martin Li**, the philanthropist director of the F.E.A.S.T. homeless shelter Peter's Aunt May volunteers at, is the masked antagonist **Mr. Negative** — the leader of a vigilante organization called the **Inner Demons** waging a coordinated campaign of revenge against Norman Osborn for an Oscorp medical-experimentation incident that killed Li's parents in his childhood. Li's coordinated theft of an Oscorp-developed bioweapon called **Devil's Breath** — designed as a targeted neural-disabling agent but biologically uncontrolled — establishes the campaign's central political threat: the bioweapon's airborne deployment would kill most of the city's population within seventy-two hours.

The campaign's third act stages **Otto's transformation into Doctor Octopus**. Otto's neural-interface prosthetic system — developed for his own progressive ALS-like motor degeneration — produces accelerating mental instability across the campaign's runtime. His coordinated assault on the Raft prison frees the city's incarcerated supervillain population — Mr. Negative, Electro, Rhino, Scorpion, Vulture — and forms the **Sinister Six** under Otto's central command. The campaign's middle-third structural decision pivots the central antagonist relationship from Mr. Negative's politically-motivated vendetta to Otto's coordinated city-spanning assault.

The climactic sequence stages Peter's confrontation with Doctor Octopus atop Oscorp Tower in the campaign's most acclaimed boss encounter. Peter defeats Otto, recovers the **Devil's Breath cure**, and is faced with the campaign's central moral choice. **Aunt May** has been infected during the Sinister Six's airborne deployment in Times Square. The recovered cure is sufficient for either Aunt May's immediate treatment or for mass-replication to treat the city's broader infected population — Peter cannot save both. He chooses the city. **Aunt May dies** in the hospital with Peter's hand on hers, the campaign's central emotional resolution staged with sustained character work between Peter and the surrogate mother who raised him. The campaign closes with Aunt May's funeral, Peter's reconciliation with Mary Jane committed, and the post-credits stinger introducing **Miles Morales** — a Harlem teenager whose own spider-bite incident during the F.E.A.S.T. crisis has produced powers identical to Peter's — for the broader Insomniac Marvel continuity's continuation.

title: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
guide: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is Respawn Entertainment's 2019 Soulslike action-adventure set in the dark times after Order 66. Padawan survivor Cal Kestis attempts to rebuild the Jedi Order while hunted by Imperial Inquisitors. The walkthrough captures the full main campaign across two parts on PS5 Pro at 4K HDR 60FPS with PSSR upscaling, no commentary. The cinematic playthrough emphasizes the Metroidvania-style world design.

chapters.name: 1. Bracca — Scrapyard Apprentice
chapters.summary:
The campaign opens with **Cal Kestis**, a survivor of Order 66, working anonymously as a scrap-cutter on the Star Destroyer scrapyard of **Bracca** five years after the Empire's massacre of the Jedi. The opening sequence is structured as a slow-burn tonal piece: Cal lives in the workers' shanty town, hides his Force sensitivity, and works alongside his friend **Prauf**, an Abednedo scrapper. The chapter dwells on the texture of a post-Jedi galaxy — the visible Imperial oppression, the rationing, and the careful concealment Cal has constructed to survive.

The chapter's pivot is a workplace accident that forces Cal to instinctively use the Force to save a fellow worker. The act is witnessed by Imperial agents, and the resulting investigation brings the **Second Sister** — a Jedi-trained Imperial Inquisitor — to Bracca personally. Prauf is murdered. Cal is chased across the scrapyard in the campaign's first sustained combat tutorial.

The chapter ends with Cal extracted from Bracca by **Cere Junda**, a Jedi survivor turned anti-Imperial operative, and her pilot **Greez Dritus** aboard the *Mantis*. The campaign's central mission — to recover a Jedi holocron that contains the names of every Force-sensitive child the Order has ever identified — is introduced.

chapters.name: 2. Bogano — BD-1 and the Vault
chapters.summary:
The campaign's tutorial planet. **Bogano** is a small, lush moon where the late Jedi Master **Eno Cordova** hid the holocron Cere has been hunting. The chapter is structured as a sustained exploration of the moon's surface, with Cal acquiring the campaign's signature companion: **BD-1**, a small spherical droid Cordova left behind to guide a worthy Jedi to the vault.

The chapter introduces the campaign's traversal fundamentals — wall-running, double-jumping, vine-swinging, and the BD-1 healing and scanning systems that will define the campaign's puzzle and exploration loop. The combat density is light; the chapter's focus is environmental learning.

The chapter ends with Cal locating Cordova's holocron vault — sealed with a puzzle Cordova specifically designed so that only a Jedi who has visited multiple Zeffo-civilization tombs can solve it. The campaign's next planets — Zeffo, Kashyyyk, and Dathomir — are introduced as Cordova's required pilgrimage sites.

chapters.name: 3. Zeffo — The First Tomb
chapters.summary:
The campaign's first sustained dungeon planet. **Zeffo** is the homeworld of the Zeffo civilization — an extinct precursor culture that practiced Force-based engineering centuries before the Jedi Order. The chapter is structured as a vertical exploration of Zeffo's surface and tomb complexes, with new traversal abilities (Force-push, slow-time effect) introduced through the Tombs themselves.

The chapter's combat highlights include the campaign's first sustained encounter with **Imperial Purge Troopers** — anti-Jedi specialists equipped with electrostaffs and shield-piercing weapons. The Purge Troopers force Cal to integrate parry mechanics and Force-redirect attacks into his combat rotation.

The chapter ends with Cal acquiring the first Zeffo tomb's puzzle piece and the campaign's exploration loop now fully open. The next destination — **Kashyyyk** — is unlocked.

chapters.name: 4. Kashyyyk — The Wookiee Resistance
chapters.summary:
The campaign's mid-act political chapter. Cal arrives on the Wookiee homeworld **Kashyyyk** during the Imperial occupation, where **Saw Gerrera**'s rebel cell is conducting a sustained insurgency against the Empire's slave-labor camps. The chapter is structured as a multi-stage rebellion assistance arc, with combat ranging from Wookiee village skirmishes to a multi-stage AT-AT walker assault on an Imperial refinery.

The chapter dwells on the campaign's political stakes. Saw Gerrera — a recurring figure across the broader *Star Wars* franchise — is rendered as a paranoid but effective extremist whose methods Cal finds alarming. The Imperial occupation of Kashyyyk is rendered with significantly more environmental detail than the franchise has typically afforded the Wookiee homeworld.

The chapter ends with the Imperial refinery destroyed, **Tarfful** (the Wookiee chieftain) freed, and the second Zeffo puzzle piece recovered from the planet's interior.

chapters.name: 5. Zeffo (Return) — Trilla's Pursuit
chapters.summary:
A return to **Zeffo** for the second tomb, with the campaign's mid-act pursuit dynamic now fully active. The **Second Sister** — revealed in audio logs as **Trilla Suduri**, a former Jedi Padawan turned Inquisitor — has been tracking Cal across the campaign's planets and now confronts him at the second Zeffo tomb. The chapter is structured as a sustained dungeon-and-duel sequence.

The duel with the Second Sister is the campaign's first sustained Inquisitor confrontation. Trilla's combat style is the campaign's most demanding to date — dual-blade lightsaber stance, Force-redirected projectile attacks, and a multi-phase fight that demands mastery of the campaign's parry mechanics. The duel ends with Cal's narrow escape, Trilla's identity as a former Jedi exposed, and the campaign's central moral question — what the Empire has done to its former Jedi — fully introduced.

The chapter ends with Cal's recovery on the Mantis, Cere visibly disturbed by Trilla's identity, and the campaign's mid-third-act setup for the next planet.

chapters.name: 6. Dathomir — The Nightsisters
chapters.summary:
The campaign's darkest sustained chapter. **Dathomir** is the homeworld of the **Nightsisters**, a witch-coven of dark-side Force users whose order was nearly extinguished during the Clone Wars. Cal arrives in pursuit of the third Zeffo puzzle piece and immediately meets **Merrin** — the last surviving Nightsister, a teenage survivor who has spent the years since her order's destruction alone among the planet's ruins.

The chapter is structured as a sustained negotiation arc. Merrin is hostile to Cal — the Jedi were complicit in the Nightsisters' fall — and the chapter requires Cal to navigate her grief through both combat and dialogue. The combat highlights include encounters with **Undead Nightbrother warriors** that Merrin's magic resurrects to test Cal's resolve.

The chapter dwells on the campaign's most thematically dense conversations — Merrin's grief, Cal's PTSD from Order 66, and Cere's own complicated history with the dark side. The chapter ends with Merrin granting Cal access to the third Zeffo puzzle piece, and Merrin herself joining the *Mantis* crew permanently as the campaign's most acclaimed companion.

chapters.name: 7. Ilum — The Kyber Crystal Pilgrimage
chapters.summary:
The franchise's most cinematic single-planet chapter. **Ilum** — the ancient Jedi pilgrimage world where Padawans crafted their first lightsabers — has been hollowed out by the Empire and converted into a weapons-research facility. Cal arrives in pursuit of the second Zeffo tomb's central key, but the chapter pivots into the campaign's most emotionally complete sequence: Cal's pilgrimage to find a new kyber crystal of his own and to complete the lightsaber his master Jaro Tapal began.

The chapter is structured as a single sustained walk through the Imperial-occupied ice caverns of Ilum, with Cal's PTSD from Order 66 surfacing through Force-vision flashbacks. The combat density is light; the chapter's central focus is the construction of Cal's new lightsaber and his emotional reconciliation with his master's death.

The chapter ends with Cal's completed double-bladed lightsaber, his Force sensitivity stabilized, and the campaign's final destination — the Inquisitorius fortress on **Nur** — staged.

chapters.name: 8. The Subterrel Crypt — Final Holocron
chapters.summary:
A medium-length chapter that returns Cal to the third and final Zeffo tomb, with Trilla's reinforced Inquisitor team now waiting at the chamber's entrance. The chapter weaves the campaign's hardest puzzles with sustained combat across the tomb's deepest level, culminating in a final dueling sequence against the Second Sister.

The chapter's duel is the campaign's emotional centerpiece. Trilla is defeated, captured, and brought aboard the *Mantis*. The chapter's resolution stages the campaign's most acclaimed conversation — Cere confronting Trilla as her former Padawan, with the campaign's full backstory of betrayal and survival now finally articulated. Cal recovers the holocron with the list of every Force-sensitive child the Jedi Order knew of.

The chapter ends with Cal in possession of the holocron, Trilla murdered by **Darth Vader** in the *Mantis* itself, and the campaign's final pursuit now committed.

chapters.name: 9. Nur — Confrontation with Vader
chapters.summary:
The campaign's climactic chapter. **Nur** — the Inquisitorius fortress moon — is where Cal has decided to confront **Darth Vader** personally to recover Cere from his pursuit. The chapter is structured as a sustained infiltration of the Inquisitorius base, with combat against Purge Troopers, Stormtroopers, and the campaign's hardest sustained enemy encounters.

The chapter's climactic encounter is the **duel with Vader** himself. The fight is mechanically distinct from every prior boss in the campaign — Vader cannot be defeated. The encounter is staged as a sustained survival sequence, with Cal forced to flee through the fortress's collapsing infrastructure while Vader pursues with overwhelming Force-based attacks. The sequence is one of the most acclaimed in modern *Star Wars* storytelling.

The chapter ends with Cal and Cere narrowly escaping Nur, Vader's pursuit halted, and the campaign's central moral question — whether to use the holocron's list to recruit Force-sensitive children into a new Jedi order — staged for the final scene.

chapters.name: 10. The Holocron Decision — Bogano Return
chapters.summary:
The campaign's epilogue. Cal returns to **Bogano** to face the final moral choice the campaign has been building toward: whether to use Eno Cordova's holocron to begin building a new Jedi order, with the catastrophic risk of the Empire identifying and hunting the children, or whether to destroy the holocron and protect them from ever being targeted.

The chapter is structured as a single sustained conversation between Cal, Cere, Merrin, and Greez aboard the *Mantis*. The decision is Cal's. The campaign's resolution stages either choice with substantial emotional weight, and the credits roll over the *Mantis* departing Bogano's atmosphere.

The chapter's post-credits scene establishes the campaign's sequel, with the surviving cast committed to a galaxy-spanning resistance arc that *Survivor* will pick up five years later.

story:
Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is Respawn Entertainment's 2019 third-person action-adventure, set in the Star Wars canon's **five years after Order 66** — the systematic Jedi-extermination protocol that terminated the Jedi Order at the close of the prequel trilogy. The campaign protagonist is **Cal Kestis**, a former Jedi Padawan who survived Order 66 as a child by using his master's coordinated sacrifice as cover for his own escape. Cal has spent the intervening years working as a scrap-yard rigger on the Outer Rim planet **Bracca**, deliberately suppressing his Force abilities and avoiding any behavior that might attract Imperial attention.

The opening sequence stages the campaign's inciting incident. Cal's coworker and closest friend **Prauf** is about to fall to his death during a routine industrial accident; Cal uses Force telekinesis to save him in front of multiple witnesses. The Empire's Inquisitorius — the order of fallen Jedi tasked with hunting surviving Jedi — dispatches the **Second Sister** and the **Ninth Sister** to Bracca within hours. Prauf is murdered by the Inquisitors as a public demonstration. Cal is rescued from the resulting chase by the crew of the **Stinger Mantis**: former Jedi Knight **Cere Junda** (whose own complicated Order 66 backstory the campaign progressively reveals), Latero pilot **Greez Dritus**, and the salvaged astromech droid **BD-1** whose recovered memory provides the campaign's central exposition.

The campaign's central artifact is a **Jedi Holocron** containing a comprehensive list of Force-sensitive children across the galaxy — children whose identification by either the Jedi or the Empire would determine whether the Order could be rebuilt or systematically wiped out. The Holocron has been hidden by Cere's former Jedi Master **Eno Cordova** in a coordinated multi-planet trail of clues only Cere's apprentice could follow. Cal's mission is the Holocron's recovery ahead of the Inquisitorius's parallel pursuit. The campaign's exploration unfolds across Bogano, Zeffo, Kashyyyk, Dathomir, and Ilum, with the franchise's signature lightsaber-combat system and the campaign's *Metroidvania*-style environmental progression rendering the planets as interconnected sustained exploration zones.

The campaign's central character reveal lands at the midpoint. **The Second Sister** — the Inquisitor pursuing the Mantis crew across the campaign — is **Trilla Suduri**, Cere's own former Jedi Padawan. During Order 66, Cere had been captured with Trilla and a group of younglings; under Inquisitorius torture, Cere broke and revealed Trilla's location to the Empire, with Trilla subsequently captured, tortured to the breaking point, and turned to the Dark Side as a sanctioned Inquisitor. Cere's lifelong avoidance of Force use is the suppressed grief over what she did to her own apprentice. The campaign's broader character work tracks Cere's slow recovery of her Jedi identity through Cal's mentorship.

The climactic sequence stages a coordinated assault on **Fortress Inquisitorius** on the Outer Rim planet Nur. Cal defeats Trilla in single combat in the Fortress's central reflection chamber. Cere — arriving moments later — speaks with Trilla in the language of their old apprenticeship and convinces her, in the campaign's most acclaimed character beat, to renounce her Inquisitorius commitments. Trilla's resulting redemption is interrupted by the arrival of **Darth Vader** himself, whose presence the campaign refuses to dramatize as a boss fight. Vader strikes Trilla down with one move, throws Cere across the chamber, and pursues Cal through the collapsing Fortress in a sustained chase sequence. Cal escapes by flooding the Fortress's central waterway, barely surviving Vader's pursuit, and the campaign closes on the Mantis's escape with the Holocron intact. Cal's final decision is the campaign's central moral resolution: he **destroys the Holocron**, refusing to position the named Force-sensitive children for either rebuilding or extermination, leaving their futures to the Force. The franchise's broader Sequel Trilogy continuity is positioned for the 2023 successor installment.

title: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor
guide: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor is Respawn's sequel to Fallen Order, set five years after the original. Cal Kestis is now a battle-hardened Jedi fighting the Empire as it tightens its grip on the galaxy. New abilities include dual-stance lightsaber styles (Single, Double-Bladed, Dual Wield, Blaster, Crossguard). The walkthrough captures the full main campaign across two parts on PS5 Pro at 4K HDR 60FPS with PSSR upscaling, no commentary.

chapters.name: 1. The Coruscant Infiltration
chapters.summary:
The campaign opens five years after the events of *Fallen Order*, with **Cal Kestis** infiltrating the upper floors of Coruscant in pursuit of **Senator Sejan**, a corrupt Imperial collaborator. The opening hour is structured as a sustained vertical infiltration of the Coruscanti skyline — Cal's traversal repertoire is fully expanded with the **dual-blade**, **double-bladed**, and reworked **crossguard** lightsaber stances introduced in the campaign's tutorial sequence.

The chapter's central event is the **Coruscant crash**. Cal's stolen Imperial shuttle is attacked by Imperial Inquisitor forces during the escape, with Cal's allies **Greez Dritus**, **Nightsister Merrin**, and **Cere Junda** scattered across the galaxy when their ship goes down. The chapter ends with Cal alone in the crashed Mantis, deep in the frontier moon of **Koboh**, with no operational support network and a galactic-scale Imperial bounty on his head.

chapters.name: 2. Koboh — Greez's Cantina
chapters.summary:
The campaign's central hub introduction. Cal awakens on **Koboh** in the care of **Greez Dritus**, the four-armed Mantis pilot from *Fallen Order*, who has spent the years between games operating a cantina in the frontier settlement of **Rambler's Reach**. The chapter is structured as a sustained exploration of Koboh's open-world territories, with Greez's cantina serving as the campaign's primary hub for the rest of the game.

The chapter's combat highlights include the campaign's first sustained encounter with **Bedlam Raiders** — a faction of mercenary scavengers led by the Imperial-aligned warlord **Rayvis**, whose army has been excavating Koboh's surface for High Republic-era technology. The Raiders introduce the campaign's most varied enemy class structure.

The chapter ends with Cal reuniting with **Bode Akuna**, a mercenary contact and family man who becomes the campaign's primary companion across its entire runtime.

chapters.name: 3. Jedha — The Hidden Path
chapters.summary:
A mid-act chapter that takes Cal off Koboh and onto **Jedha**, the desert pilgrimage moon glimpsed in *Rogue One*. The chapter opens with Cal arriving at the **Crypt of Uhrma** — a hidden Jedi sanctuary that **Cere Junda** has spent the years between games turning into a refugee center for force-sensitives and former Jedi. Cere's introduction is the campaign's first emotional anchor.

The chapter's central reveal is **Tanalorr** — a Jedi sanctuary world hidden in the Abyss between systems, accessible only via High Republic compass technology. The Hidden Path's purpose is to evacuate force-sensitives to Tanalorr before the Empire's purge reaches them. The chapter's exploration loop opens Jedha's pilgrim districts, the ruins of the former Imperial outpost, and the High Republic-era Crypt of Uhrma's deeper chambers.

The chapter ends with Cal in possession of the High Republic compass fragment, the campaign's central mission established, and the Hidden Path's broader network introduced.

chapters.name: 4. The Mantis Hangar — Bode's Family
chapters.summary:
A character-focused chapter that establishes the campaign's emotional core. **Bode Akuna**'s daughter **Kata** is introduced through Cal's visit to the family's hidden domestic life — a quiet bunker beneath Koboh's surface. The chapter dwells on Bode's relationship with his daughter, his deceased wife's connection to Cere's order, and the family's reasons for choosing to escape the Empire entirely rather than fight it.

The chapter's tone is deliberately gentler than the campaign's surrounding action sequences. The combat density drops; the dialogue depth increases. The chapter establishes the audience's investment in Bode's character before the campaign's third-act reversal will demand it.

The chapter ends with Cal committed to helping Bode and Kata reach Tanalorr alongside the rest of the Hidden Path.

chapters.name: 5. The Shattered Moon — High Republic Excavation
chapters.summary:
A mid-game vertical-traversal chapter set on the **Shattered Moon**, a remnant of a destroyed planet in the Koboh system. The chapter is structured as a sustained climbing-and-platforming sequence across the moon's broken surfaces, with new traversal abilities introduced — air-dashing, wall-clinging, and the **BD-1 grappling line** extension.

The chapter's combat highlights include the **Forest Array** sequence — a vertical Imperial transmitter complex that Cal traverses from base to summit while engaging Imperial troopers, droids, and the campaign's first sustained encounter with **Raider Lieutenants**. The traversal density and combat intensity escalate the campaign's mid-section significantly.

The chapter ends with Cal recovering a fragment of the High Republic excavation records, the existence of Tanalorr's defenses confirmed, and the campaign's mid-act open expansion of the Koboh open world.

chapters.name: 6. The Crypt of Uhrma — Dagan Gera
chapters.summary:
The campaign's first sustained antagonist introduction. **Dagan Gera**, a High Republic-era Jedi locked in bacta stasis beneath the Crypt of Uhrma since the fall of the Republic, is revived during Cal's exploration of the deep sanctuary. Dagan's introduction is initially staged as a possible ally — a Jedi master from the era of the High Republic, fluent in Force techniques the Empire's purge erased.

The chapter dwells on Dagan's slow revelation. The High Republic was not the idealistic golden age Cal has been taught; Dagan's order had its own crimes, its own betrayals, and Dagan himself was condemned by the Council for breaking the Jedi code. His freedom is the chapter's gift to him; his rage at his own order is the campaign's mid-act antagonist.

The chapter ends with Dagan revealed as the campaign's secondary antagonist, declaring his intention to seize Tanalorr for himself and his Raider army, and committing to defeating Cal across the rest of the campaign.

chapters.name: 7. Nova Garon — Imperial Fortress
chapters.summary:
The campaign's most demanding combat chapter. **Nova Garon** is an Imperial fortress moon serving as the headquarters of the Imperial Inquisitor's pursuit of Cal. The chapter is structured as a sustained infiltration of the fortress, with multiple Inquisitor confrontations, Stormtrooper platoons, and the campaign's first sustained AT-ST and TIE pilot encounters.

The chapter's central boss confrontation is the duel with **Inquisitor Drya Thornir** in the fortress's central command chamber. Thornir's combat style is the most demanding the campaign has staged, with multiple lightsaber stance switches and Force-based environmental attacks demanding mastery of the campaign's full repertoire.

The chapter ends with Thornir defeated, the Imperial pursuit of Cal significantly disrupted, and the campaign's mid-third-act assault on Tanalorr now positioning itself.

chapters.name: 8. The Mountain Ascent — Bode and Cal
chapters.summary:
A character-focused mid-third-act chapter staged across **Koboh's central mountain range**. Cal and Bode travel together on what the campaign frames as a routine reconnaissance mission, with the chapter dwelling in their friendship — Bode's stories about Kata's childhood, Cal's reflections on his master Cere, and the slow buildup of the campaign's central trust before its central betrayal.

The chapter's exploration loop opens the campaign's hardest puzzle dungeon — the **Lucrehulk wreckage** in the mountain's caldera, a Trade Federation-era warship that crashed during the Clone Wars and has been a Bedlam Raider stronghold ever since. The dungeon weaves traversal-based puzzles with the campaign's deepest single combat encounter.

The chapter ends with the wreckage cleared, the Tanalorr compass fully recovered, and the campaign's final reveal positioned for the next chapter.

chapters.name: 9. The Bode Betrayal
chapters.summary:
The campaign's central twist. **Bode Akuna** is revealed to be an Imperial deep-cover agent, planted in the Hidden Path under false pretenses with explicit instructions to recover the Tanalorr compass for Imperial use. The chapter is structured as a single sustained sequence: the revelation, the duel, Cere's death at Bode's hand, and Cal's emotional collapse.

The Bode-versus-Cal duel is the campaign's most acclaimed single confrontation. Bode is a Force-sensitive — kept hidden from Cal across the entire campaign — and his combat ability matches or exceeds Cal's. The duel ends with Bode escaping in the Mantis, Cere dying in the Crypt of Uhrma at Cal's side, and Tanalorr's location now in Imperial hands.

The chapter ends with the campaign's central question fully reframed: not whether Cal can save the Hidden Path, but whether he can become the man capable of stopping Bode before the Empire reaches Tanalorr.

chapters.name: 10. The Abyss — The Run to Tanalorr
chapters.summary:
The campaign's climactic act. Cal, **Merrin** (returned to active partnership), and the surviving Hidden Path forces stage a desperate run to Tanalorr through the **Abyss** — a hyperspace anomaly that destroys any ship not equipped with the High Republic compass. The chapter is structured as a sustained pursuit through hyperspace, with multiple Imperial intercepts and the campaign's most spectacle-heavy aerial sequences.

The chapter's combat highlights include the campaign's first sustained spaceship combat sequence, with Cal piloting a stripped-down Mantis through the Abyss's gravitational anomalies. The chapter's central tension is whether Bode's Imperial fleet or Cal's Hidden Path will reach Tanalorr first.

The chapter ends with Cal arriving at Tanalorr seconds ahead of the Empire, the Hidden Path's refugees secured on the surface, and Bode arriving alone on the planet for the campaign's climactic duel.

chapters.name: 11. Tanalorr — The Final Duel
chapters.summary:
The campaign's climactic chapter. **Tanalorr** is rendered as the campaign's most visually distinct location — a verdant Jedi sanctuary world untouched by the Empire's purge, with ancient High Republic architecture integrated into a thriving biosphere. The chapter is structured as a sustained pursuit-and-duel across the planet's central temple complex.

The final duel with **Bode Akuna** is one of the franchise's most acclaimed boss fights. Bode's combat style mirrors Cal's — both trained in similar Jedi traditions, both Force-sensitive, both emotionally invested in their separate causes — with the duel's emotional weight equal to its mechanical demands. The fight ends with Bode defeated and Cal forced to make a choice the campaign has been building toward: kill Bode, or attempt redemption.

The chapter ends with the player's chosen outcome played out in full, **Kata Akuna** processing the death of her father in front of Cal, and the Hidden Path's refugees beginning their new lives on Tanalorr.

chapters.name: 12. Epilogue — The Mantis Crew
chapters.summary:
The campaign's epilogue is staged on Tanalorr in the days following the final duel. The surviving cast — Cal, Merrin, Greez, Kata, and the Hidden Path's leadership — settle into the planet's new reality. The chapter dwells on the cost of the campaign on each character, with quiet conversations between Cal and Merrin about the future of the Jedi tradition, between Cal and Kata about Bode's legacy, and between Cal and Greez about what comes next.

The chapter's final scene establishes the franchise's third installment, with Cal departing Tanalorr on a mission the campaign deliberately leaves unspecified. The credits roll over the Mantis's departure into hyperspace. The campaign's central question — whether a Jedi can survive in an Empire that has spent two decades hunting his order — is answered, at least for now, in the affirmative.

story:
Star Wars Jedi: Survivor is Respawn Entertainment's 2023 PS5/PC sequel to *Jedi: Fallen Order*, set **five years after** the previous campaign's events — the canonical date **9 BBY**, five years before the events of *A New Hope*. The previous campaign closed with **Cal Kestis** destroying the Force-sensitive children Holocron in the Mantis's escape from Fortress Inquisitorius, his survival against Darth Vader staged with deliberate ambiguity, and the broader Jedi-resistance infrastructure positioned for his continuing mission. Survivor opens with Cal in his late twenties, scarred by the intervening years, and operating as one of the **Hidden Path's** most experienced resistance operatives.

The opening sequence stages a coordinated Imperial-archives heist on Coruscant. Cal infiltrates the Imperial Security Bureau's central tower in pursuit of classified Imperial intelligence on the **Pau'an** species's coordinated genocide — information that the broader Hidden Path resistance needs to organize a humanitarian-evacuation operation. The mission goes wrong, with Cal's resistance team killed by the **High Republic-era Imperial Senator Sejan**, and Cal himself narrowly escapes Coruscant aboard the crippled Mantis. He arrives on the frontier planet **Koboh** — a sustained open-zone environment that anchors the campaign's central exploration loop — and meets the mercenary **Bode Akuna**, a sharpshooter whose stated commitments to his eight-year-old daughter **Kata** make him the campaign's central supporting character.
